trigger_condition.shape_trigger: Selected dimension size is small and the index value equals or exceeds that dimension size, causing an out-of-range index.
trigger_condition.memory_trigger: Compiled Inductor kernel may perform an out-of-bound read when the bounds check is omitted.
trigger_condition.value_trigger: Index value equals the selected dimension size, outside the valid range [0, dim_size - 1].
trigger_condition.state_trigger: torch.compile with Inductor backend is used instead of eager execution.
trigger_condition.execution_trigger: Compiled forward pass executes torch.index_select with an invalid index tensor.
trigger_condition.concrete_constraints: x.shape=(2,2,2,2), dim=0, index=torch.tensor([2]); torch.compile(backend='inductor'); torch.no_grad() inference on CPU.

root_cause.description: Inductor-generated kernels may not perform the same index bounds checks as PyTorch eager mode; a constant propagation pass was fixed to preserve index validation semantics.

bug_oracle.description: Compiled execution returns a tensor with unexpected values instead of raising an IndexError for an out-of-range index.
bug_oracle.signal: Returned tensor contains invalid values while eager execution raises IndexError.

harness_strategy.input_mutation: Generate index tensors with values at or beyond the selected dimension boundary, such as dim_size or -dim_size - 1, across different shapes.
harness_strategy.tensor_construction: Construct input tensors with small selected dimensions so out-of-range indices are easy to trigger and detect.
harness_strategy.constraint_injection: Run the same indexing operation in eager mode and torch.compile(backend='inductor') mode, enforcing error-behavior parity for invalid indices.
harness_strategy.operation_sequence: Wrap indexing operations such as torch.index_select in a torch.nn.Module and execute under torch.no_grad with both eager and compiled modes.
harness_strategy.oracle_construction: Use eager execution as the reference; if eager raises IndexError, the compiled execution must also raise, otherwise flag incorrect output or potential out-of-bound access.
